environment.working_tree: Modified worktree (50 paths): Products planning/evidence, Catalog adapter/tests and local migrations; no Supabase remote writes or migration applications.

decisions.summary: Use current LoopDev/Rivera light-theme tokens and reusable Platform primitives; do not copy Rivera pages, hand-pick a palette or create parallel primitives.
Use official Inter for UI and JetBrains Mono for technical data in the visual source; current Geist/Geist Mono runtime usage is implementation drift to reconcile in Platform.

Products is the user-facing ERP module and the direct product/service list entry point; the standalone catalog index is removed from the proposed user flow while legacy IDs/contracts/routes remain compatible.

Products uses a single master for finished products, raw materials/components and services; the product base has a general category and each SKU variant has its own category; drafts may omit category but activation requires it; item class is independent of purchase/sale/inventory uses; finished products allow buy/make/both sourcing, raw materials/components are buy-only for now, services have no sourcing, and variants inherit product sourcing; semimanufactured items await Manufacturing discovery.
Each variant/SKU has its own independently assigned category; the approved SKU editor shows the product category as context and a separate SKU category control.
The Product Owner selected a dedicated responsive category-management view within Products, with visible return navigation and no nested drawers.
The first release is Products and categories on desktop/mobile web; Overview is navigation compatibility only.
Product Owner approved the current conceptual visual source, including Products/SKU/category and media compositions, on 2026-10-25; runtime comparison remains post-implementation.

Platform and ERP must reconcile legacy Catalog form implementation/documentation during build and verify the approved page composition uses existing shared form primitives; this is implementation evidence, not a new conceptual-approval request.
Desktop and mobile web are required; native iOS/Android are deferred for this release.
Product Owner approved the supplemental desktop/mobile SKU editor showing each SKU's own category separately from the product's general category.
The Product Owner chose upload and existing-asset reuse inside the Product gallery, with a contextual selector and no separate library route.
The Product Owner chose to retain originals and create a proportion-preserving optimized image up to 1600 px plus a 400 px thumbnail, without cropping.
The Product Owner chose separate catalog.cost.read and catalog.cost.manage permissions; access behavior remains subject to access design.

actions: Audited current ERP routes and source-backed UI/form primitives against UI and shell references, tests, active tracks, global forms status and the Product Owner-confirmed official typography.

Applied the Product Owner's VD-ERP-013 choice: added a dedicated category-tree management composition for desktop and mobile web, with visible return navigation and no nested drawer.

Revised the original five SVGs to use the exact light HSL token snapshot from src/index.css, the white shared sidebar and selected-route treatment from Sidebar.tsx, current LoopDev navigation labels and borderless SurfaceCard shadows.
Added a sixth responsive SKU editor wireframe to close the evidence gap for each variant's independently assigned category; the Product Owner approved this addendum.

Added desktop/mobile product-media wireframes for the approved in-gallery existing-asset selector and original/1600 px/400 px rendition presentation; the Product Owner explicitly approved this media addendum on 2026-10-25.
Previewed the revised standalone SVGs in the browser canvas; this is visual artifact review only, not application-runtime evidence.

Recorded implementation/documentation drift: Geist runtime typography, current catalog form composition, native select, duplicated detail section, read-only drawer mode, nested drawers and Overview fetch states.
Updated platform scope/evidence and workspace README without changing production code.

Recorded approvals separately for the original compositions, SKU-category addendum and media addendum; no application runtime was started.

The Product Owner explicitly reapproved the current design and visual artifacts after the changed-input invalidation; runtime comparison remains a post-implementation gate.
